target.title: fix(teams-meetings): stalled setup probes stay within deadline
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users checking Microsoft Teams `chrome-node` talk-back prerequisites could leave the remote node synchronously blocked beyond the setup check's 10-second budget when multiple prerequisite probes stalled.

The setup path runs `system_profiler` followed by two or three command probes. Giving every child the full 10-second timeout allowed the total blocking time to grow to 30–40 seconds, even though the caller's `nodes.invoke` deadline is 12 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Teams node host now shares one absolute 10-second deadline across the device and command probes, passes only the remaining budget to each child, and does not start another probe after the deadline expires. This matches the existing Zoom meeting node-host behavior and does not change configuration or public APIs.

## User Impact

Stalled or missing Teams audio prerequisites now fail within one setup budget instead of accumulating a separate 10-second wait for every probe. The remote node is less likely to remain blocked after the Gateway-side setup request has already timed out.

## Evidence

- Red proof with the production hunk reverted: the deadline test observed `[10000, 10000, 10000]` instead of `[10000, 7000, 3000]`, and the expired-deadline case incorrectly returned `{\"ok\":true}`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/teams-meetings/src/node-host.test.ts extensions/teams-meetings/src/runtime-setup.test.ts extensions/teams-meetings/src/node-invoke-policy.test.ts`: 3 test files passed, 5 tests passed.
- Targeted extension `oxlint` passed for both changed files.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- Node 24's `spawnSync` contract defines `timeout` per child process and blocks until that child exits, confirming that sequential full-budget calls can accumulate wall-clock blocking time.
